primary.step: Build KITE=3, a Rules-based rollout controller for the queen while an enemy knight is within SIM_RANGE (start 300): every such turn simulate about 27 candidate commands for SIM_H=5 turns with cr.core.Rules (the 24 kite headings re-aimed each turn, stand/top-up on the touched own tower, BUILD on the nearest own tower, the defence rule's site, and the current rule ladder's own output), score = our HP lost minus SIM_KILL x enemy knight HP removed by our towers, with KITE=2's hard constraints kept (end under own tower cover, outside enemy tower range), and replace the rule ladder's command only when the best candidate beats it by >= SIM_MIN_GAIN (1 HP). First deliverable: the sim adapter (seat from the start corner, player swap, a prediction test on the 180 recorded Gold games, a micro-benchmark of Rules.resolve on recorded crowds) plus the controller replacing only kite() and the under-threat stand/flee block; the defence rule and pre-contact decisions follow as phases 2-3.

primary.evidence: Where the HP goes (code reader, trace_levers section 1, trace_quirks D-E; 180 Gold games): 8615 contact turns of 38252 (47.9/game, 23%); knight damage 4038 of the 4156 HP lost; kite steps 2679 HP (7325 turns, 0.37/turn, 0.97/turn when the nearest knight is <= 120), standing/fleeing in reach 755 HP (291 turns at 2.55-2.63/turn), defence walk+build 581 HP (541 turns at 1.0-1.3/turn). Lost races vs won: kite 16.5 vs 9.4 HP/game, defence 4.7 vs 1.8, in-reach stand/flee 3.5 vs 1.5; deaths 33.8 / 5.7 / 14.8; margins median 13 (10 of 42 within 5); per game, half the kite HP >= the margin in 8 of 42 lost races, stand+defence in 8 of 42, kite whole in 22 of 42. After a kite step a knight is still within 250 next turn in 5754/7292 (79%): the step itself sheds nothing (knights 100 vs queen 60), the fight is decided by tower kill speed and pack tightness. First wave (firstwave reader q7/q8, 115 races): lossK20 = 1.88 x adjacent turns (R2 0.89); adjacent turns 5.17 vs 2.07; damage rate at contact median 6 vs 10; ttk explains 43% of adjacency variance; towers hit one creep per turn, so the fight's position relative to the towers (damage 3 at the edge, up to 5-6 near a 700-HP tower's centre) and the number of covering towers set the kill rate; the static rule has no such term. Collision order matters (seat reader toy port of Physics/Rules: a standing queen takes 19 HP as P0 vs 36 as P1 over 12 turns from 4 knights; fleeing cuts 48 -> 26 and 25 -> 18): kite() cannot see it, Rules reproduces it. Cost model (code reader): 5 collision passes x E(E-1) sqrt pairs, E = creeps + 2 + nSites (<= 24); creeps alive median 12 at t25 (max 16), 2-4 at t50-200 (p90 8-11, max 20) -> 4.4k-7.8k pairs per simulated turn typical, 15k worst, estimated 0.05-0.3 ms (unbenchmarked); 27 x 5 = 135 turns per real turn -> 7-40 ms worst, against a free budget of about 30 ms (50 - 7.7 measured max - 10 margin) -> the work budget or a local sub-state (entities within 600) must be sized by the benchmark. Everything the horizon needs is in the local view except enemy gold and the enemy queen's intent: barracks progress (InputReader lines 81-84), tower HP/range, creep HP; spawns within 5 turns are exact. History (history reader): the two largest arena steps were queen-under-knights changes undervalued locally (v08 KITE=2 S 0.667 -> +2.46; v12 anchor 0.5716 -> +3.28); the one that left cover (v07 KITE=1, S 0.680) gave -0.71.
primary.lossMode: HP race first wave and midgame (the 47.9 contact turns per game; 54.8 and 28.5 kd/game against >= 20-rated opponents), queen death by siege (9) and attrition (8): in the deaths' last 10 turns 182 of 290 turns were kite moves (13.7 HP per death); vs strong opponents, who stand more (MOVE 0.67) and lose 0.70 HP per contact turn while we kite 85% and lose 0.47 over nearly twice the contact turns.
primary.expectedGain: Addressable per game: the in-reach excess (2.63 and 2.55 vs 0.97 HP per turn) = 473 HP / 180 = 2.6 HP; the defence walks 3.2 HP (581/180), of which perhaps a third is avoidable; 10-20% of the kite pool = 1.5-3 HP; together 3-5 HP/game, concentrated in lost races (24.7 HP/game in the three pools vs 12.7 in won races). Per-game flips (the code reader's bounds, not a uniform addition): 6-10 of the 42 lost races (= 6-10 of 180 games, +3-5 pp win rate) plus 2-4 of the 17 siege/attrition deaths, so +3-6 pp realistic, +8 pp upper. Local: S 0.55-0.62 against v12 on the mirror is the expectation (v08's kiting rewrite scored 0.667 against v07; v12's 3.5-HP first-wave saving 0.5716 against v11). Arena: the class's arena/h2h ratio was 2.7-3.7 (v08, v12), so a visible step (>= M 2.46) is plausible but not assured; the plain logistic conversion gives only +0.4-0.8 points for +3-6 pp at Gold scale 3.04. The structural payoff is the road: the defence build-or-not (phase 2), the pre-contact retreat and the second-tower timing (phase 3, horizon 10-15 for 3-4 macro candidates), enemy-tower avoidance and the idle-queen tower maintenance become candidates or evaluation terms of one controller instead of a new flag family each, and the same adapter gives the project its first opponent-motion model.
primary.effort: New subsystem, 3-5 days. Day 1: adapter and tests (seat, player swap, enemy queen WAIT, preallocated states), a prediction test replaying v12's 180 Gold games through InputReader (cgAttribute-style) and comparing the 1-turn and 5-turn predicted HP loss and knight positions with the recorded next turns, and a micro-benchmark of Rules.resolve on recorded crowds (t25 crowds of 12-16 creeps). Days 2-3: controller, warm-up extension, unit tests on captured death windows (918143669 t201-211: 11 top-ups under 7-10 knights at 4-5 HP/turn; 918168604 t197-234; 918150876). Day 4: development sweep. Day 5: screen. The artifact grows little (Rules, Physics, GameState already ship); procCheck on both seats repeats as for every artifact.
primary.p2Plan: Development sweep on seeds 1 + 397k (500 maps, both seats) against v12, field and rival: arms SIM_H 3/5/7 x SIM_RANGE 250/300/400 x SIM_KILL 0/1 (1 = 25 knight HP, one kill, worth 1 queen HP) with the cover constraint hard, plus one arm with it soft (3-HP penalty) to reproduce v07's failure deliberately; alongside S report HP per contact turn, in-reach stand turns, deaths per 1000 maps, LocalProfile first-wave loss and contact distance, LegScan max play() time and simulated turns per real turn (a queenSteps-like counter), and the number of deadline cuts (must be 0). Pick one arm by S with no G4/G5 regression. Screen on fresh block screen-pv3 k=6 (seeds 1006000000 + 397 i, i < 2000; boss on the first 500 at 3 threads, 200 ms): G0 no slow turn > 50 ms, with the work budget sized so the worst recorded crowd takes <= 15 ms on a performance core (3x margin for the laptop's efficiency cores and CG's single CPU; a 2-thread repeat with identical games settles host noise as before); G1 mirror lower CI > 0.50 on 2000 maps (the HP-race sensor: 91% of mirror games reach turn 250); G2 boss >= -2 pp; G4 field >= -2 pp (17 waves per game, the most contact turns; the opponent where v08's kiting showed +13.7 pp); G5 rival >= -2 pp (the kiting, giant-playing death sensor). The effect shows on the whole panel because all three send knight waves. A pass looks like: G0 clean, S >= 0.55 with HP per contact turn down >= 15% and deaths per 1000 not up, field delta >= 0, max play() <= 20 ms in LegScan. Then the final evaluation on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) against v12, procCheck -Popp=v01 (seeds 5000) and -Popp=boss (6000) with no SLOW line, and the user's upload decision (recommendation S >= 0.60; the class's arena record argues for an upload at 0.55-0.60). Pre-screen for free before coding the controller: an arena-replay diff (cgAttribute with the flag over replays/arena/v12/gold/upload-01 and -02) counting the turns and games where the rollout's command differs, split by the 42 lost races, 29 deaths and 109 wins.
primary.risks: (1) G0 and tail latency: CG runs one CPU with an unknown JIT state, and Rules has never run inside the artifact's warm-up, so a cold rollout at the first contact (turn ~24) could exceed 50 ms; mitigations are the warm-up extension, the deadline cut, LegScan tail times and procCheck on both seats. (2) Model mismatch: the enemy queen WAITs in the sim (she MOVEs on 44-51% of turns; within 5 turns only her top-ups matter), enemy TRAINs are unknown (they spawn >= 5 turns later), and the stdin order of creeps may differ from the referee's internal order used in collision resolution; the prediction test decides, and a biased simulator would be worse than the static rule. (3) Horizon myopia: one 700-HP tower needs about 24 turns to kill a 4-knight pack (one target per turn), so 5 turns see only damage dealt; a large SIM_KILL can make her stand to farm tower damage and bleed, the v07-type artefact the stand-still local opponents reward; keep the cover constraint hard and the kill weight small in phase 1. (4) Panel bias: field never kites and rewards any mobility, rival kites and plays giants in 85% of its games, the mirror over-weights races; the panel predicted +1.0 for v07 and the arena gave -0.71, so after an upload the arena mechanism metrics (share of contact turns at own towers, 90% for v12; HP per contact turn 0.47) must be checked, not only the placement. (5) Reproducibility: a time-budgeted search makes repeated bench runs produce different games; hence the fixed work budget with the deadline as a counted safety cut. (6) The history of per-step tweaks is flat (STAND_REACH 155 neutral, KITE_PULL 200 neutral, KITE_MAX nothing): the rollout's new content is exact knight motion, collision pushes, tower damage rates and the stand-versus-step trade; if the development sweep shows <= 2 HP/game of saving, the subsystem still pays as the platform for phases 2-3, but that is a decision for the user after day 1's prediction test and benchmark, before the controller is written. (7) Effort creep: phase 1 stays in-contact only; pre-contact triggers and the defence rule are later phases.

runnerUp.step: Add an open-loop wave model, knightEta(s): the turn when the enemy's knights (the ones alive, at 100 per turn, and the ones a visible enemy knight barracks will spawn in 5 - progress turns) reach our queen or the tower she would hold, and gate two existing decisions on it: (a) in the first-wave window, walk to the second tower site only if its build completes >= ETA_MARGIN (2-3) turns before the ETA, otherwise pump the first tower (ETA_PUMP_TO=500 instead of 700) and hold at it; (b) after the window, abort a ladder, mine or barracks walk and return to the nearest own tower that covers her when the ETA is shorter than the turns to finish the walk plus one build plus the return, resuming when no knight is within 500 (clearOfKnights). This is the structural alternative when the rollout subsystem is not affordable: the same prediction, done as arithmetic instead of simulation and search.
runnerUp.mechanism: New rule (about 80 lines) in MainBot.play before the ladder (rule 5, lines 148-163) and in the touch rule's top-up threshold (line 121, TOWER_HP replaced by ETA_PUMP_TO while towers < 2 and a wave is coming): knightEta over s.cx/cy with Const.CREEP_SPEED[KNIGHT] = 100 and the enemy knight barracks' barrProgress/barrTraining (InputReader lines 81-84 set them from p1; CREEP_BUILD_TIME 5), the walk time from the existing MainBot.walkTurns / Physics.queenStep or RoutePlanner's plan length; flags WAVE_ETA=1, ETA_MARGIN, ETA_PUMP_TO, ETA_RETREAT=1, ETA_SPELL_MAX (a cap per spell like KITE_MAX). It differs from the rejected WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM (static tower counts that skipped all top-ups, so both towers sat at 200 HP and the first one melted, summed tower HP at t50 1464 vs 1648, deaths doubled) by the time criterion and by keeping the first tower's HP; it differs from LADDER_CLEAR or KITE_RANGE 500 (distance triggers; v07's 500 lost 12 pp against field by leaving the ladder) by acting only when the wave arrives before the walk can finish, on the 2-3 turns of warning the traces show. No collision simulation and no candidate search; phase 3 of the primary would replace it with simulated candidates, so nothing is wasted if both are built.
runnerUp.evidence: First wave (firstwave reader q7/q8/q9, 115 races of v12's 180 Gold games): second tower turn minus contact <= -3: lossK20 1.1 HP, 24% lost (n=21); [-3,0): 2.7 HP, 21% (28); [0,3): 6.9 HP, 36% (39); >= 3: 11.6 HP, 63% (27); the contact turn is the opponent's barracks timing (corr 0.77; mean contact 18-20 for a barracks at turns 1-5, 24-26 at 7-8, 27-28 at 13-16), while our second tower completes at turn 25 in both groups (25.2 vs 24.9): a fixed schedule meets an opponent-driven arrival that the input announces (the enemy barracks' progress p1 every turn). One-tower regime (24 lost / 25 won): the new tower completes 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after contact (p=0.008), 2.9 vs 1.7 walk turns under knights; against >= 20-rated opponents the second tower before contact won 11/19 vs 11/39 at or after. Early-barracks opponents (first barracks <= turn 8): 42 games, S 0.50, contact 22.5, 1.24 towers at contact. Midgame (midgame reader deep3 and C:/Users/garus/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bb685f0a5e96cb91/cdd060ad-818d-46d6-8fa6-5d79a4fb541f/scratchpad/designer/recost.py over midgame/games.json): 153 walking-caught episodes in the 42 lost races cost 456 of 598 kd; the warning (a knight within 500, none within 250) lasts a median 2 turns; the nearest own tower (median 136 away) is reachable before contact in 141/153 episodes (92%, 329 of 456 kd), 237/248 in won races, 86/95 in deaths (641 of 849 kd). Re-costed per game at the pooled at-tower rate by wave size (maxK 1-5: 0.0/0.14/1.21/3.9/16.9 kd per episode): the saving is 6.4 HP per lost race but only 2-3 of 42 lost races flip at 50-100% of the saving (918145702 -3 with 6.1 saved, 918148351 -2 with 4.8; the other close ones have ~0 walking HP), against 17.9 HP per death with 13 of 29 deaths saving >= 10 HP (918158663 70, 918152893 47, 918148069 46, 918150491 42, 918164892 41, 918164775 40, 918146052 38, 918151685 37) and 2.7 HP per won race.
runnerUp.lossMode: (a) HP race first wave and vs strong opponents (they build the barracks early, so the wave arrives before our fixed second tower); (b) queen death by siege and attrition (the walking-caught episodes of the 29 deaths carried 849 of their 1306 P2-P5 kd) and HP race midgame secondarily.
runnerUp.expectedGain: (a) Counterfactual on the arena games: 8 of the 24 one-tower lost races flip if their lossK20 fell to the two-tower mean, 9 of the 31 second-tower-after-contact races if to the before-contact mean of 2.0 (about +4-5 pp before costs; symmetric exposure 6 of 25 won one-tower races). (b) 13 of 29 deaths save >= 10 HP; the deaths are economic collapses (opponent income >= 2x ours in 23 of 29), so a saved 10-70 HP buys turns rather than wins: if a third survive to the limit, +2-4 games; the close lost races gain 2-3. Realistic total 6-10 of 180 games (+3-5 pp); local S 0.53-0.58 against v12 (v12's own first-wave change scored 0.5654 on the screen and 0.5716 in the evaluation for a 3.5-HP saving); on the arena the first-wave class paid 2.7-3.7x its local S (v08, v12), so a step near M = 2.46 is plausible, with the lower placement risk of a flag whose fallback is v12's behaviour.

Screen the single best arm on screen-pv3 k=6 (seeds 1006000000 + 397 i, i < 2000; k=7 if the primary took 6): G0; G1 mirror lower CI > 0.50 (first contact at turn 24 with one tower: the regime the rule targets); G4 field >= -2 pp (contact at 21 with one tower; the binding gate: the static flags lost 3-9 pp here and v12 itself -1.49 pp); G5 rival >= -2 pp (contact at 25; kiting and giants); G2 boss as a formality (0.0000 deltas in the last six screens). A pass looks like: S lower CI > 0.50 with t2rel shifted negative by >= 2 turns in the mirror, lossK20 down from 4.3 to <= 3, summed tower HP at t50 within 100 of v12's, deaths per 1000 not up against field, field delta >= -2 pp; report per seat (the rules' tilt costs seat 1 the first wave: 8.38 vs 5.01 HP, and flags have moved the seats by 5-6 pp differently). Pre-screen first: the arena-replay diff over v12's 180 Gold games, counting in how many of the 42 lost races and 29 deaths the ETA gate would have changed a command.
runnerUp.risks: The family was rejected twice (2026-11-05 against v08, 2026-11-07 against v11) with a recorded mechanism: two towers met the wave but the mean loss did not fall (7.3/8.2 vs 7.8), the first tower stayed at 200 HP and melted, deaths doubled; the ETA gate's fallback is v12's play (pump and wait), so the regression is bounded to the games where the ETA says 'in time' and is wrong, but the local one-tower loss (5-7 HP) is smaller than Gold's (10.2 in lost races), so the screen may show S 0.52-0.55 for a change the arena rewards, as v12 did (0.5716 -> +3.28). The ETA ignores collisions and sites (knights slowed by obstacles, the queen's own blocked path), so the margin must absorb +-1-2 turns. Part of the t2rel gradient is opponent quality (strong players build early; within >= 20-rated opponents the cell is 19 vs 39 games) and the kill-speed -> adjacency -> loss chain is inferred (the recorded first-10-turn tower damage differs only 5.06 vs 5.59, p=0.06). The retreat (b) delays the ladder (23.5 yellow-zone turns per lost race, 12% of turns 50-249) and the mirror punishes lost tempo; cap the spell and exempt the first-wave window, where WAVE_ANCHOR's tower must be built with the wave visible. The per-game re-costing shows (b) does not flip the close lost races (2-3 of 42), so its gain rests on the deaths, where survival also needs the economy; G4 is the gate most likely to fail, as for v12.

whyNotOthers: TRAIN_SYNC relaxation (SYNC_WAIT_MAX, kill-shot release, DUMP_FROM 230): the strongest cheap army flag by evidence (8082 of 38252 turns, 21%, held with 80-159 gold and two barracks; gold >= 80 at the end of 23 of 42 lost races; 1281 kill-shot turns in 37 games), but its realistic gain is 2-4 games of 180 (+1-2 pp) because the released 4 knights must cross 4-9 enemy towers, v06 adopted the sync for a measured reason (0.548 vs 0.49 without it), and the panel has never ordered army changes with the arena (v10 -0.20); it is not a structural step and belongs as a bundled companion flag in the same artifact as either proposal, where a bundle is what the arena's resolution (M 2.46 at two placements) can see. Post-ladder economy and tower maintenance (pump the lowest tower, never at the 800 cap; mine interleave; a Legend-style balance): the waste is real (52.4 pump turns per game beyond the third on one tower, 24.7% of turns alive, against 20.5 for strong Gold and 10.6 for Legend; summed tower HP 2378 vs 2800 at t200 despite 92.5 vs 69.5 top-ups) and the 29 deaths are economic collapses (opponent income >= 2x ours in 23 of 29), but the 42 lost races are against turtles with our economy (maxIncome 7.7 vs 8.3 in won races), every economy arm failed locally for a recorded structural reason (our half's sites are towers at ladder completion, late mines are far), PV3/PV5 record that the panel cannot measure late economy, and only an arena exception could judge it; the tower-maintenance part (own sites only) is the one new mechanism and is the natural phase-2 idle-time term of the rollout, not the next step. Seat-aware hedging (DEFENCE_FWD on seat 1, an adjacency rule): the tilt is the referee's collision order (the repository fix of 2018-04-28 never reached the live game) and can only be hedged; halving v12's seat gap is worth +0.25-0.4 Gold points, inside M, and the per-seat flag effects (+5-6 pp between seats) are about 2 SE on one 500-map block; worth per-seat reporting in bench_pair and a free re-read of the existing reports, not a step. Enemy-tower-aware flight and idle pump: 114 HP over 180 games (2.7% of the HP lost), one lost race decided (918150190, td 7 = the gap); a near-certain targeted fix to bundle with either proposal (the rollout's enemy-range penalty contains it), not a step. LADDER_CLEAR as a pure distance rule: subsumed by the runner-up's time-based retreat, and the per-game re-costing shows its value is in the deaths (17.9 HP per death), not in the close races (2-3 of 42 flip), so the midgame reader's uniform +4..+6 HP estimate (9-10 flips) overstates it. Giants, archers, RELEASE_NEAR and larger merged releases against queen-safe opponents: the enemy queen is outside her towers' ranges on 0.2-0.9% of turns, giants cost 21 pp against rival, archers were noise, and no local opponent plays Gold's tower-covered queen, so the arena alone could judge them; the lever is the opponent's to deny. Panel and process levers (rival?GIANTS=0, a FieldBot first-wave knob calibrated to Gold's 11.4 HP, shorter boss series, the arena-replay pre-screen, per-seat reporting): they improve how a step is judged, not the bot, and the pre-screen and per-seat report should accompany both proposals rather than replace them.
